Rejected an attractive but unsupported structure: a 'rationale quality score' aggregating reason weights and evidence grades. No consulted primary source supports aggregation across those scales, so weighting is recorded as asserted values only and the aggregation question is logged as a gap.

Ownership sweep against the relation ledger: every bundle, layer, finding and function was re-read against the WM-ACT-032 and WM-KNW-008 rationales and against each outgoing reference. Approval execution, record disposal execution, evidence appraisal, claim structure, judicial reasoning, change-request lifecycle and rule evaluation were each found to be referenced only; where a draft concept drifted towards ownership — notably follow-up obligations and audit trails — it was reduced to an identifier-only reference and restated in out_of_scope or a boundary note.

Evaluation and enforcement test: the quorum function was deliberately renamed to attest rather than verify, and its effects state that no threshold computation or enforcement is performed. The integrity function verifies a digest but writes an outcome entry rather than acting on it, and the access layer emits classifications and instructions while enforcement is assigned to an external system.

Artefact collision test: the four artefacts introduced here (dr-gov-art-authority-register, dr-gov-art-lifecycle-ledger, dr-gov-art-access-schedule, dr-gov-art-disposition-record) were checked against the ten pre-existing core and reasoning artefact identifiers; none is re-created, renamed or shadowed, and dr-rsn-art-dissent-record is referenced by identifier only.

Identity falsifiability test: every artefact identity strategy and every local identifier was checked for date-derived or period-derived components. Serial names use a zero-padded sequence scoped to the decision master record, and the timestamp rule explicitly refuses bare dates, second-less times and offset-less times.

Exclusive representation test: each of the thirteen findings was checked to have either non-empty artefacts with a null rationale or an empty artefacts array with a substantive rationale; nine are inline-only with reasons that turn on reference-graph shape, personal-data minimisation or avoidance of duplicating an externally owned document.

Counterexample search for structure: a separate voting-record structure, a minutes artefact, an interests-register artefact and an implementation-tracking layer were each considered and rejected, because in every case an external owner already holds the concept and no primary source supported placing it here.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two distinct axes must not be conflated. On the record plane the frozen registry value `standalone-mm` classifies how vr.wm-knw-010 sits in the Vercy registry — a self-standing meta-model entry rather than a fragment, mixin or alias of another entry — and it is absent from the subject-model enum, so it is retained as registry metadata and never used as the subject kind. On the subject-model axis `aggregate` is the most defensible schema kind and is affirmed: the model declares one root identity (the authoritative master-system decision identifier), and alternatives, screening records, criteria, evaluation rounds, outcome fields, reasons, argument elements, bindings and ledger entries are addressable only through that root, with artefact names derived from it. Immutability after approval, append-only ledger patching and versioned supersession define a single consistency boundary over that cluster, which is precisely aggregate behaviour. `entity` was rejected as understating an owned multi-part cluster; `event` was rejected because occurrent semantics (convening, deliberation, voting, approval execution) are explicitly assigned to WM-ACT-024 and the subject here persists, versions, is reviewed, reopened, retained and disposed; `relationship`, `classifier`, `mixin`, `registry` and `pattern` each describe referenced machinery (profiles, code lists, external registers) rather than the governed subject.

decisions.concept: Subject-model entry kind for WM-KNW-010
decisions.rationale: One root identity governs an internally owned cluster of alternatives, criteria, evaluation rounds, reasons, argument elements and ledger entries under a single immutability and version boundary; entity understates the cluster and event would collide with the occurrent semantics assigned to WM-ACT-024.

decisions.concept: Frozen registry value standalone-mm
decisions.disposition: retained on the record plane only
decisions.rationale: It classifies the registry record rather than the modelled subject and is not in the schema enum, so it is preserved as registry metadata while the subject kind is taken independently; the two axes coexist without contradiction and both are stated in the published draft.

decisions.concept: Splitting decision content from rationale into separate models
decisions.rationale: Rationale artefacts derive identity from the decision master identifier and rejection reasons hang off core-owned alternatives, so a split would sever the single consistency boundary that justifies the aggregate kind; the existing internal core, reasoning and governance split already routes ownership.

decisions.concept: Merging WM-KNW-010 into registry parent WM-KNW-007 Claim
decisions.rationale: A claim asserts that something is the case while a decision selects among registered alternatives and produces a disposition with effect timing, conditions and consequences; generic assertion machinery cannot host alternatives, criteria, evaluation rounds or outcome dating.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root identity and artefact identity priority
decisions.rationale: The master-system identifier ranks first, DMN's document-scoped xsd:ID is demoted to an alignment with a recorded conflict, dates, meeting names, titles and file paths are refused as identifiers, and Dimension-assigned ULIDs are retained permanently as aliases when a master identifier later appears.

decisions.concept: Serial artefact-kind discriminator registry
decisions.rationale: The serial naming rule registers only GOVLED, GOVACC and GOVDIS, yet four serial artefacts outside governance — comparison matrix, sensitivity record, dissent record and explanation rendition — rely on unregistered artefact-kind keys, so collision-freedom is asserted rather than demonstrated.

decisions.concept: Sequence scope of dr-rsn-art-dissent-record
decisions.rationale: Its identity strategy scopes the zero-padded sequence per dissenting party while the service-layer rule states the sequence scope is explicitly the decision master record; the two readings produce different names for the same artefact and must be reconciled to one scope.

decisions.concept: Ownership assignments to neighbours absent from the relation ledger
decisions.rationale: Delete rules assign disposition execution to WM-REC-010 and boundary notes defer approval, judgment and claim machinery to WM-ACT-024, WM-POL-021 and WM-KNW-007, but the frozen contract registers only the WM-ACT-032 inbound and WM-KNW-008 outbound relations.

decisions.concept: Parent relation to WM-KNW-007 and duplicated identity machinery
decisions.rationale: The registry names WM-KNW-007 as parent but the ledger records no such relation, while this model defines its own identity, version discriminator, supersession, provenance and lifecycle; whether that specialises or duplicates parent-owned assertion machinery cannot be settled from the frozen contract alone.

decisions.concept: Missing producing function for the statement of reasons
decisions.disposition: gap recorded, not repaired in this mode
decisions.rationale: dr-rsn-art-statement-of-reasons has no governed function that records a reason or issues the statement, whereas every other major artefact has a producing function; add_functions must remain empty under the waiver, so the gap is logged for the next pass rather than filled here.

decisions.concept: Self-referential boundary note naming WM-KNW-010 as its own neighbour
decisions.disposition: reclassified as an internal split note
decisions.rationale: Listing the model as its own neighbour pollutes the neighbour contract used for boundary checking, while the content itself is a valid statement about core, reasoning and governance routing and should be labelled as an internal split rather than an external boundary.

decisions.concept: Removed 40 CFR 1502.14 and 1505.2 as content pattern
decisions.disposition: accepted with a mandatory historical-only label
decisions.rationale: The pack itself records the CEQ interim final rule removing parts 1500 to 1508 effective 11 April 2025, so the no-action baseline and record-of-decision content bind only as a profile-conditional historical pattern and must never be rendered as a current government-wide requirement.

decisions.concept: Duplicate registration of the GDPR as SRC-005 and SRC-033
decisions.rationale: The entries are the original OJ text and the 2016-05-04 consolidation of one instrument; without an explicit expression label they inflate apparent source breadth and permit divergent citations of the same article across findings.

decisions.concept: Retention, legal hold and authorised erasure ordering
decisions.disposition: accepted as a declared jurisdictional profile
decisions.rationale: Hold blocks disposition, tombstone-first preserves identity, authority, status and disposition facts, and an authorised erasure may reduce the tombstone; the model declines to resolve the statutory conflict globally and assigns it to the adopting Dimension's records and privacy authorities, which is the defensible position.

decisions.concept: Deny-by-default access against access-to-documents presumptions
decisions.rationale: The pack concedes the default will understate disclosure duties for public bodies unless an access profile is bound, but discoverable register metadata, partial release by redaction and five named exceptions keep the understatement visible rather than silent.

decisions.concept: No local evaluation, execution or enforcement
decisions.rationale: The quorum function attests rather than computes, the integrity function writes a verification outcome without acting on it, the assumption re-check only annotates status, and rule execution, access enforcement and audit-trail generation are consistently assigned to external systems.

bundles.name: Decision framing and identity
bundles.description: How a specific decision is identified, typed against a jurisdictional profile, and framed by its question, objectives, context, constraints and the rules it relies upon.
bundles.rationale: DMN's Decision element carries question and allowedAnswers, its objectives and impacted indicators, and its information and knowledge requirements; ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 relates a decision to the concerns it addresses and the elements it affects; appraisal guidance requires a case for change, SMART objectives and critical success factors before options are considered. Framing must therefore be modelled before alternatives, and it is the part of the decision that determines what a complete record looks like.

layers.name: Decision identity and classification
layers.description: Stable identification of the decision content, discrimination between its expressions, and its classification against a decision type and jurisdictional profile.

findings.name: Decision identity and version discriminator
findings.description: How one governed decision is stably identified, how successive expressions of the same decision are discriminated, how the identity of the decision content is kept distinct from the identity of the record that carries it, and how supersession and alternate jurisdictional identifiers are recorded.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is reference data carried directly on the decision record: identifier values, a version discriminator, typed links to superseded decisions and labelled alternate identifiers. No separate governed artefact is produced, and any rendered identifier block belongs to the carrying record model rather than to decision content.

findings.name: Decision type, jurisdictional profile and required content
findings.description: Classification of the decision against a controlled decision-type scheme, binding of the jurisdictional or institutional profile that governs its required content, and declaration of the content elements that profile makes mandatory.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Typing and profile binding are code values plus a derived list of required element names. They are structured reference data evaluated against published code lists held by the profile custodian; producing a separate artefact would duplicate the code-list registry rather than add governed content.

layers.name: Decision question, objectives and context
layers.description: What the decision is being asked to settle, what it is intended to achieve, and the context, dependencies and affected subjects within which it is taken.

findings.name: Decision question, triggering issue and admissible answer space
findings.description: The single question the decision answers, the admissible answers to that question, the problem or issue that made the decision necessary, and whether the question decomposes into required sub-decisions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The question, its admissible answers and the problem statement are short authored text fields plus typed references. DMN carries them as simple string children of the Decision element, and holding them inline keeps the answer directly comparable with the recorded outcome statement without a separate artefact to keep in step.

findings.name: Objectives, success factors and expected effects
findings.description: The objectives the decision is intended to achieve, the critical success factors any acceptable option must satisfy, the indicators expected to be affected and the horizon over which effects are expected.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Objectives, success factors and indicator references are short structured statements bound directly to the decision. DMN models supportedObjective and impactedPerformanceIndicator as element references rather than documents, and the indicator definitions themselves are governed by a measurement model, so no artefact is produced here.

findings.name: Decision context, dependencies and affected subjects
findings.description: The subjects, populations, assets or system elements the decision affects, the extent over which it applies, the input data and upstream decisions it depends on, the concerns it addresses and the assumptions declared about its context.

layers.name: Constraints and applied decision rules
layers.description: The binding conditions any outcome must satisfy and the declarative rules the decision relies on to map inputs to admissible outcomes.

findings.name: Binding constraints and admissibility conditions
findings.description: The hard conditions any selected alternative must satisfy, their declared values and units, the separation of binding constraints from soft preferences, and the treatment of an alternative that violates one.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Constraints are short structured statements with a binding flag, an optional quantified limit and a citation. They are read alongside the criterion set during screening, and holding them inline avoids a second place where a limit could drift out of step with the criterion that measures it.

findings.name: Applied decision rules and conflict-resolution policy
findings.description: The declarative rules the decision relies on to map stated inputs to admissible outcomes, the declared policy for overlapping rules, the versioned reference to any external rule source, and whether the outcome was rule-determined or discretionary. Statement-level only: executing the rules is the work of a decision service outside this model.

bundles.name: Alternatives, screening and evaluation
bundles.description: The candidate alternatives placed under consideration including any required baseline, the screening that determines eligibility, the criteria and weights used for comparison, and the recorded evaluation results.
bundles.rationale: Appraisal and decision-analysis guidance treats the alternative set as a governed object in its own right: HM Treasury requires a longlist narrowed to a shortlist with business-as-usual always carried forward, NEPA practice required inclusion of the no action alternative and recorded reasons for eliminating others, and NASA requires screening against mandatory criteria before scored evaluation. Criteria, weights and results are therefore modelled separately from framing and from the outcome, so that a comparison can be inspected and re-run without touching the framing or the recorded answer.

layers.name: Candidate alternatives and eligibility
layers.description: Registration of the alternatives under consideration, including any profile-required baseline, and the screening that admits or excludes each from detailed evaluation.

findings.name: Candidate alternative set and mandatory baseline
findings.description: The alternatives placed under consideration, how each is identified and described, whether a no-action or business-as-usual baseline is present as the profile requires, and how variants of one alternative are distinguished from genuinely distinct alternatives.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Alternatives are append-only structured records held on the decision: an identifier, a kind code, a description and a variant link. They must stay directly addressable from evaluation results and from the outcome, so extracting them into a separate artefact would add an indirection with no governance benefit.

findings.name: Eligibility screening and recorded exclusion
findings.description: The screening or mandatory criteria that decide whether an alternative proceeds to detailed evaluation, the recorded reason for each exclusion, the stage at which it occurred, and the conditions under which an excluded alternative could be reinstated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Screening produces a status and a short recorded reason per alternative, held directly on the alternative it concerns. The regulatory requirement is that reasons for elimination be briefly discussed, not that a separate screening document exist, and the screening activity itself belongs to the referenced decision-making activity model.

layers.name: Criteria and evaluation results
layers.description: The declared basis for comparing alternatives and the recorded results of applying it, including aggregation, ranking and sensitivity.

findings.name: Evaluation criteria, measures, scales and weights
findings.description: The criteria against which alternatives are compared, each with its measure, scale, unit and direction of preference; the separation of mandatory pass-or-fail criteria from compensatory trade-off criteria; and the weighting scheme where one is used, including the declared weighting method.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The criterion set is a declared list of definitions, scales, directions and optional weights, addressed by identifier from every evaluation result. It is reference data whose value lies in being fixed and directly citable; the workshop or panel that derived weights is an activity governed elsewhere, and named decision-analysis methods bind as external references rather than as content held here.

findings.name: Evaluation results, comparison and sensitivity
findings.description: The recorded result of each alternative against each criterion for one evaluation round, any aggregation and ranking derived from those results, the sensitivity of the ranking to changed scores, weights or assumptions, the evidence cited by reference in support of results, and the status of contested or provisional results.

bundles.name: Selection, disposition and stated consequences
bundles.description: The alternative selected, the disposition and explicit outcome statement that answers the decision question, and the conditions, reservations and consequences the decision states as part of its own content.
bundles.rationale: A record-of-decision pattern requires the decision to be stated, the alternatives considered to be identified, the preferable alternative to be named, the factors balanced to be discussed, and mitigation and monitoring conditions to be declared or their absence explained. ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 adds that making a decision can raise new concerns. The outcome is therefore modelled as governed content in its own right, distinct from the approval that authorised it and from the record that publishes it.

layers.name: Decision outcome and attached conditions
layers.description: The explicit answer to the decision question with its disposition and applicability, and the conditions, unresolved matters and consequences stated as part of the decision.

findings.name: Selected alternative, disposition and outcome statement
findings.description: Which alternative is selected, the disposition the decision reaches, the explicit outcome statement that answers the decision question, the declared onset and applicability of effect, the factors expressly balanced, and any explained divergence from the evaluation ranking.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The outcome is a small, immutable set of fields on the decision itself: a selected-alternative reference, a disposition code, the statement answering the question and the declared effect times. The published record of decision that renders these fields is a document governed by the record model, and the approval that authorised them is an activity governed elsewhere, so producing an artefact here would claim ownership of one or both.

findings.name: Attached conditions, unresolved matters and stated consequences
findings.description: The conditions, mitigations and safeguards attached to the outcome as part of the decision itself, the matters expressly left unresolved or reserved, the consequences and accepted risks the decision states, the declared reopening or review triggers, and the new concerns or follow-on decisions the decision raises.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions, reservations and stated consequences are declarative clauses of the outcome and must travel with it in any projection. Where a decision directs a monitoring or compliance plan, that plan is an implementation artefact owned by the change and activity models; recording it here as an artefact would take ownership of execution and monitoring that this model explicitly disclaims.

bundles.name: Stated reasons and argument structure
bundles.description: The reasons offered for a decision and the argument that connects premises, inference schemes and conclusions to the recorded outcome, including contrastive reasons for not selecting alternatives and any explicitly asserted causal or counterfactual reasoning.
bundles.rationale: Structured-argument standards consistently separate the asserted conclusion from the inference link that supports it and from elements that conflict with it, while the EU duty to state reasons makes the stated reason itself a governed object attached to a legal act. Keeping the offered reason and the argument connecting it to the outcome as separate, independently citable structures prevents a narrative summary from being mistaken for a checked inference.

layers.name: Stated reasons and rejection reasons
layers.description: The rationale statement issued with a decision, the discrete reason records that compose it, and the contrastive reasons recorded for alternatives that were not selected.

findings.name: Rationale statement and constituent reasons
findings.description: The holistic statement of reasons issued with a decision together with the discrete, independently citable reason records that compose it. Each reason carries its type, its polarity relative to the recorded outcome, an optional asserted weight on a named scale, and the party asserting it. The statement explains the decision; it does not restate the decision problem, option set or criteria, which the `core` split owns.

findings.name: Reasons recorded for rejecting alternatives
findings.description: Contrastive reasons attached to alternatives that were considered but not selected: the ground of rejection, any recorded condition whose change would have made the alternative selectable, and whether the rejection is stated as final for this decision or as a deferral. The alternatives themselves, their definitions and their evaluation against criteria are owned by the `core` split and are referenced, not restated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Rejection reasons are reference-and-qualifier records that hang off alternatives owned by the `core` split. Materialising them as a separate artefact would create a second place where an alternative's definition could be restated and drift from the governed option set, and would invite consumers to read a rejection note as an independent evaluation. They are therefore carried as inline bindings on the referenced alternative and surface only inside the statement of reasons and explanation renditions produced elsewhere in this model.

layers.name: Argument structure and inference
layers.description: How premises, conclusions, inference-scheme references, critical questions and asserted conflict relations are represented, and how explicitly asserted causal or counterfactual reasoning is recorded without being upgraded beyond what was stated.

findings.name: Premises, conclusions and inference-scheme references
findings.description: The argument connecting reasons to the recorded outcome, represented with the inference itself as a first-class element rather than as an implicit edge. Covers the role each element plays (premise, conclusion, context, exception), the inference scheme referenced for each step, recorded critical questions and their responses, the support status of each premise, and asserted conflict relations. The model records asserted inference only and performs no validity or entailment evaluation.

findings.name: Asserted causal and counterfactual reasoning
findings.description: Records causal and counterfactual reasoning only where the decision record explicitly asserts it: the causal statement, the strength qualifier used, the antecedent varied in a counterfactual and the outcome claimed to follow, the evidential basis cited, and any competing explanation or confounding considered. The model never upgrades an observed association into an asserted cause, and no consulted standard supplies a normative structure for counterfactual rationale, so this finding is carried as an assertion record with declared limits.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Causal and counterfactual assertions have no artefact of their own: they are qualifiers on reasons and premises already carried elsewhere in this model, and no consulted primary standard defines a normative document form for them. Producing a separate artefact would give an asserted causal claim standing independent of the reason it qualifies and would invite it to be cited as an established finding. The content is therefore kept inline on the reason or premise record, marked as asserted, and this finding is flagged as an evidence gap in coverage rather than presented as canonical structure.

bundles.name: Grounding, appraisal and epistemic qualification
bundles.description: How rationale elements bind to governed claims and evidence, how the decision authority's own appraisal of that evidence is recorded separately from the evidence body's certainty grade, and how assumptions, dependencies, uncertainty, trade-offs, sensitivity and contestation are qualified.
bundles.rationale: Every consulted framework separates the evidence from the appraisal of it and from the reason it is offered for: certainty-of-evidence frameworks grade a body of evidence, citation ontologies type the rhetorical act of citing, and regulatory-analysis guidance requires assumptions and sensitivity to be disclosed separately from the recommendation. This bundle carries the bindings and epistemic qualifiers required to explain a decision without absorbing the evidence or claim models.

layers.name: Claim and evidence bindings
layers.description: Reference bindings from rationale elements to governed claims in WM-KNW-007 and governed evidence in WM-KNW-008, carrying the role, citation type, locator and stance but never a copy of the referenced content.

findings.name: Claim references used as premises and conclusions
findings.description: Bindings that place a governed claim into an argument role, pin the claim version relied on when the reasoning was asserted, and mark any local paraphrase as a restatement. Claim identity, wording, revision and verification status remain in WM-KNW-007; this finding owns only the binding and the role the claim plays in one argument.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A claim binding is pure reference data: an identifier, a version pin, a role code and an optional marked paraphrase. Giving it an artefact would produce a second store of claim text outside WM-KNW-007 and create exactly the duplication the reference relation exists to prevent, since a materialised binding document would age independently of the governed claim. The binding therefore lives inline on the argument element and is projected only inside the argument structure export owned by the argument-structure finding.

findings.name: Evidence citation bindings
findings.description: Bindings from a reason or premise to a governed evidence item in WM-KNW-008, carrying the citation type drawn from a governed vocabulary, a locator pinpointing the relevant part of the cited resource, the stance of the citation, and whether the citation was made by the decision author or inherited from an intermediate source. Evidence content, acquisition, custody and grading remain in WM-KNW-008.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A citation binding must remain a reference, a type code, a locator and a stance. Materialising it as an artefact would tempt implementers to embed the cited excerpt and thereby create an uncontrolled copy of evidence whose identity, custody and grading belong to WM-KNW-008, breaking the reference contract and producing a second evidence store that can drift or outlive its source. Locators are held inline precisely so that resolution always goes back to the governed evidence item.

layers.name: Appraisal, assumptions and confidence
layers.description: The decision-local appraisal of cited evidence, the assumptions and dependencies the reasoning rests on, and the confidence and uncertainty qualifiers attached to reasons, inferences and the rationale as a whole.

findings.name: Decision-local appraisal of cited evidence
findings.description: The decision authority's own judgement of how far cited evidence bears on this decision: the weight given to it here, the sufficiency judgement recorded for the reason it supports, and the stated preference where bodies of evidence conflict. The evidence item's intrinsic certainty grade and the grading methodology belong to WM-KNW-008 and are carried by reference; this finding never re-grades evidence and never asserts that the appraisal is correct.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The appraisal is a decision-local qualifier on an existing citation binding, not a document. Emitting it as an artefact would produce something that reads like an evidence assessment report and would compete with the grading that WM-KNW-008 owns, blurring exactly the distinction this finding exists to preserve between the evidence, its intrinsic grade and one decision's judgement of its bearing. Keeping it inline forces every reader to encounter the appraisal attached to the specific reason it qualifies.

findings.name: Assumptions, dependencies and defeat conditions
findings.description: Statements the reasoning rests on that are recorded as assumed rather than supported, the external conditions, inputs and third-party commitments the reasoning depends on, the conditions under which an assumption would be considered defeated, the period or context for which it is asserted to hold, and the party recorded as responsible for its continued validity. This model records assumptions; it does not monitor, test in production or enforce them.

findings.name: Uncertainty and confidence qualifiers
findings.description: Confidence qualifiers attached to reasons, inferences and the rationale as a whole: the scale used, whether the qualifier is about the evidence, the inference or the outcome holding in practice, the stated limits of knowledge beyond which the reasoning should not be relied on, and how a verbal qualifier maps to any numeric range. The model records the qualifier as asserted and does not compute or validate calibration.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Confidence is a qualifier on something else — a reason, an inference, an appraisal or the whole rationale — and has no standing apart from what it qualifies. Extracting qualifiers into their own artefact would detach a confidence level from the statement it modifies, which is the specific failure mode calibrated-language guidance exists to prevent, and would let a summary confidence figure circulate without its scale definition or knowledge limits. Qualifiers are therefore inline and always travel with their subject and scale reference.

layers.name: Robustness and contestation
layers.description: Recorded trade-offs and sensitivity of the reasoning to its inputs, and the counterarguments, counter-evidence, objections, dispositions and dissenting or minority positions recorded against it.

findings.name: Trade-offs and sensitivity of the reasoning
findings.description: What was traded against what, which disbenefits are recorded as accepted, which inputs or assumptions would change the recorded outcome and within what range, any switching value at which the preferred option would change, and whether the varied inputs are disclosed well enough for a qualified third party to reproduce the finding. This model records the results and the disclosure; it does not run the analysis.

findings.name: Counterarguments, objections and dissent
findings.description: Counter-arguments and counter-evidence recorded against a reason or inference, who raised them, how each was dispositioned in the rationale, which argument elements are marked defeated by a recorded challenge, and any minority or dissenting position preserved as an attributed statement rather than folded into the majority rationale. Adjudication authority, approval workflow and role assignment stay with the `governance` split.

bundles.name: Explanation and reasoning provenance
bundles.description: Explainable decision traces and bounded, audience-scoped explanation renditions produced from the recorded rationale, together with the provenance of the reasoning itself and the separation of authored rationale from machine-generated explanation.
bundles.rationale: Explainability guidance requires an explanation to be meaningful to its recipient and accurate to the process that generated the output, and EU law gives affected persons a right to clear and meaningful explanations of an AI system's role in a decision. A provenance vocabulary supplies the attribution terms, including software agents, needed to say who or what produced the reasoning. This bundle separates the rendition given to an audience from the reasoning it renders and from the provenance of that reasoning.

layers.name: Decision traces, renditions and reasoning provenance
layers.description: The ordered trace from inputs to recorded outcome, the bounded renditions produced for declared audiences with their faithfulness and omission statements, and the provenance of the reasoning including authorship mode and generating agent.

findings.name: Explainable decision trace and bounded explanation renditions
findings.description: The ordered sequence of reasoning steps recorded as the trace from inputs to the recorded outcome, and the audience-scoped explanations produced from it. Each rendition declares its audience, what was omitted or replaced by a reference, the rationale revision it renders, and an assertion that it reflects the recorded reasoning rather than a post-hoc narrative. A rendition is an explanation, not an audit record: audit trails and access logging are owned by the `governance` split.

findings.name: Reasoning provenance and authored versus generated rationale
findings.description: Who or what produced the recorded reasoning: whether it was authored by a person, generated by a software agent, or generated then edited; which agent, model version and configuration produced any machine-generated text; what prior rationale, template or precedent it was derived from; and the separation of the time the reasoning was asserted from the time the record was observed or ingested. Machine-generated explanation must be labelled so that it is never read as an authored reason.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Reasoning provenance qualifies every other record in this model rather than standing on its own: authorship mode, generating agent and the two timestamps must travel with the reason, appraisal, objection or rendition they describe, or the labelling requirement for machine-generated content fails exactly where it matters. A separate provenance artefact would also duplicate the agent and activity records that the provenance vocabulary places outside this model, and would let a rendition circulate stripped of its generated-content label. Provenance is therefore carried inline on each record and projected into artefacts as attribution metadata.

bundles.name: Decision authority, mandate and participation
bundles.description: Establishes who was competent to take the decision, under which mandate and delegation, who is accountable for the resulting record, who participated in which declared role, and what integrity conditions applied to that participation.
bundles.rationale: A decision is only authoritative if the deciding body acted within a mandate and the participation conditions prescribed for it. ISO 15489-1 makes assigned responsibilities and mandate-driven records requirements a precondition of authoritative evidence; PROV qualifies responsibility, association and delegation; the Council's Rules of Procedure show mandate, quorum and proxy representation as explicit, recorded facts.

layers.name: Mandate, deciding authority and accountable roles
layers.description: The competence chain: the authority that decided, the instrument that empowered it, the delegations exercised beneath it, and the standing roles accountable for the decision record afterwards.

findings.name: Deciding authority and mandate binding
findings.description: Identifies the body, office or role that took the decision and binds it to the mandate instrument, its subject and jurisdictional limits, its validity window and its succession path. Records the authority as an attributable agent rather than as free text.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and proxy representation
findings.description: Records the chain from the mandate holder to the person or system that actually exercised the decision, with the ceiling and validity window on each step, whether sub-delegation was permitted, and how a vote or act exercised on behalf of another participant is captured.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Delegation facts are short reference structures resolved against dr-gov-art-authority-register and mirrored into the lifecycle ledger; they carry no independent document body. The delegation instrument itself is a document owned and published by the issuing authority, so materialising a second artefact here would duplicate an external record and create a competing copy of a mandate this model does not own.

findings.name: Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer assignment
findings.description: Assigns the standing accountabilities over the decision record after it is taken: who owns it, who maintains its governance metadata, who holds physical or logical custody of its projections, and who is obliged to review it. Distinguishes accountability for governance metadata from accountability for the substance of the decision.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Role assignments are reference tuples pointing at party identifiers held in an external identity model; they have no document body of their own and change independently of the decision content. Materialising them as an artefact would create a stale local copy of party master data and a second, competing source of truth for accountability that the adopting Dimension's role catalogue already owns.

layers.name: Participation, decision rule and integrity of participation
layers.description: Who took part in which declared capacity, under which decision rule and participation threshold, and what was declared, determined and acted upon regarding conflicts of interest.

findings.name: Participant roster, declared roles and applicable decision rule
findings.description: Captures the participants and their declared roles, the entitlement to vote or object, the decision rule that governed the taking of the decision, the mode of proceeding, and the attestation that any required participation threshold was met.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The participation surface is a roster of references plus a small set of coded assertions; the narrative proceedings that would justify a document already exist as minutes or a proceedings record owned by the convening body and, where reasoning is involved, as the reasoning area's artefacts. Holding these facts inline keeps them queryable and avoids creating a rival account of the sitting that this model has no authority to issue.

findings.name: Declared interests, conflict determination and recusal
findings.description: Records interests declared by participants before or during the decision, who determined whether a declared interest was disqualifying, the recusal or mitigation action taken, and the effect of recusal on the applicable participation threshold.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Declarations and determinations are short, strongly typed assertions that must remain individually queryable for threshold recomputation and disclosure masking, and they frequently contain personal data whose minimisation is easier to enforce at field level than in a document body. Where a jurisdiction requires a standing register of interests, that register is an external instrument owned by the integrity authority and is referenced rather than reissued here.

bundles.name: Approval, status lifecycle and change control
bundles.description: How the decision moved from submission through review to approval or ratification, which validity state it holds and why, how it may be reviewed, appealed, reconsidered or reopened, and how its versions, changes and content provenance are controlled.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative decision records require an explicit, transition-controlled state model with recorded effective dating, a supersession and consolidation chain, and attributable change history. RFC 2026 demonstrates staged maturity, retirement to a historic state and a bounded appeals procedure; the ELI ontology supplies in-force, consolidation and repeal relations; Akoma Ntoso supplies FRBR-level version identity and lifecycle events; PROV-O supplies attribution, revision and invalidation.

layers.name: Submission, approval, status and reconsideration
layers.description: The approval pipeline binding, the controlled status and validity model with its effective dating and conditions, and the triggers and windows for review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening.

findings.name: Submission, review and approval stage binding
findings.description: Records which governance stages the decision passed, which are mandatory before it can take effect, and the identifier of the external approval or ratification activity that evidences each stage. Distinguishes approval from ratification and from non-binding endorsement.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Stages are carried as thin bindings to approval activity records that live in WM-ACT-024; the substantive approval evidence, including approver identity, execution and completion, is that model's artefact. Creating a governance document for the pipeline here would reproduce an approval record this model does not own and would introduce a second, divergent statement of whether approval occurred.

findings.name: Status, validity and conditional effectiveness
findings.description: Holds the controlled status of the decision and its permitted transitions, the separation of approval, publication and effective instants, the conditions attached to a conditional decision and who confirms them, and identifier-only references to follow-up implementation or monitoring obligations.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status, effective dating and conditions are the queryable control fields that determine whether the decision may be relied upon at a given instant, so they must be first-class inline data rather than text inside a document. Follow-up obligations are deliberately reference-only because implementation progress, monitoring results and outcome measurement are executed and evidenced by other models; issuing an artefact here would invite those execution facts to accumulate locally.

findings.name: Review, appeal, reconsideration and reopening
findings.description: Defines what triggers a scheduled or event-driven review, who may appeal or seek reconsideration to which forum within what time limit, on what grounds a closed decision may be reopened and what status it then takes, and how a review outcome is linked to the original decision without overwriting it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Triggers, windows, forums and outcome links are scheduling and relationship data that must drive obligations and queries rather than be read out of a document. The substantive review or appellate determination is itself a decision or a legal judgment owned by another record, so this finding deliberately holds only the pointer and the relation type and creates no artefact that could be mistaken for the determination.

layers.name: Version history and provenance of decision content
layers.description: The authoritative version chain with supersession and consolidation, the append-only ledger of governance changes with attributable agents and separated time axes, and the provenance of the governed decision content itself.

findings.name: Version identity and append-only change ledger
findings.description: Establishes which version is authoritative, which prior versions it supersedes or consolidates, and an append-only ledger of governance changes recording the acting agent, the reason, the authority relied on, the significance of the change and the separated event, observation and ingestion instants.

findings.name: Provenance of the governed decision content
findings.description: Records which agents generated, revised and attested the governed content in which qualified roles, from which prior drafts or decisions it was derived, how cited claim and evidence records are referenced without restatement, and whether the record was created natively or imported.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance here is a graph of typed references between agents, activities and prior records, and is most defensible when held as data that can be projected into an interoperable provenance vocabulary. The narrative products it points at — the statement of reasons, the reasoning trace and the evidence records — are artefacts already owned by the reasoning area and the evidence model, so no new document is warranted.

bundles.name: Access, integrity and defensible disposition
bundles.description: How the decision and its governance metadata are classified for access and disclosure, how their integrity is anchored and linked to external audit trails, and how they are retained, held and defensibly disposed of.
bundles.rationale: Records remain authoritative only if their integrity is demonstrable, their accessibility is controlled and their disposition is defensible. ISO 15489-1 makes integrity, usability and appraisal-driven disposition constitutive of an authoritative record; NARA organises requirements around maintenance, disposal and transfer; NIST separates access enforcement, audit and disposal into controls owned by the operating system; Regulation 1049/2001 and the GDPR supply the disclosure and erasure profiles.

layers.name: Access classification, disclosure and integrity assurance
layers.description: The classification and disclosure schedule for each part of the decision, the exemptions and partial-access rules that apply, and the fixity, sealing and audit-linkage facts that make the record's integrity demonstrable.

findings.name: Access classification, exemptions and disclosure schedule
findings.description: Sets the access class for the decision and, separately, for its rationale and governance metadata; records the exemption grounds relied on to withhold, whether partial access by redaction is possible, when an embargo lapses, what register-level metadata stays discoverable, and which personal data must be minimised before disclosure.

findings.name: Fixity, sealing and audit linkage
findings.description: Records the digest algorithm and value sealing each governed version, who computed it, which signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidences non-repudiation of the approval, how a failed verification is reported without altering the sealed version, and which external system holds the audit trail.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Integrity facts are small, machine-checkable values attached to versions and must be verifiable independently of any document rendition; a document would itself need sealing and would create a recursion. Crucially, the audit trail that these values correlate to is generated, protected and retained by an external system, so this finding holds references only and does not materialise an audit artefact whose semantics this model does not own.

layers.name: Retention, legal hold and defensible disposition
layers.description: The retention schedule binding and its trigger, the legal hold state, the authorisation and evidence for disposition, the surviving tombstone facts and the archival transfer path for records of permanent value.

findings.name: Retention binding, legal hold and defensible disposition
findings.description: Binds the decision record to a retention schedule and its start trigger, records whether a legal hold is in force and by whom, states which facts survive when deletion is authorised and which model executes disposition, evidences destruction or transfer, and identifies records of permanent value destined for archival transfer rather than destruction.

model.name: Commercial Contract
model.purpose: Give agents the context needed to identify, form, read, operate and close a legally binding commercial agreement between two or more parties as a jointly owned record, independent of storage format.
model.scope_statement: Covers the agreement record itself: its identity and classification, the party positions and their authority, how it was concluded and executed, the structure and terms of the agreed text, the obligations and schedule it creates, the record of performance, non-performance, remedy, change, notice and termination, and the governance of that record (provenance, integrity, access, retention, interoperability). Scope is business-to-business commercial contracting, following the HCCH Principles' scope of parties acting in the exercise of their trade or profession. External legal norms, the real-world identity of the parties, procurement award processes and dispute proceedings are referenced, not duplicated.
in_scope: Agreement identity, subject-matter classification and the applicable legal regime declaration
Party positions, their roles, legal identification and signing authority
Formation facts: offer, acceptance, conduct, standard-term incorporation, execution and effectiveness
Addressable clause structure, constituent document set, precedence and authentic language
Commercial terms: price and payment, delivery and risk transfer, warranty, liability and protective terms
Obligations expressed as deontic specifications with bearers, source clauses, violations and reparations
Milestones, due conditions, cure periods and performance/acceptance records
Non-performance, excuse, remedy, amendment, assignment, notice, termination and survival
Record governance: provenance, integrity of the executed text, access, retention, disposition and projections
out_of_scope: Consumer contracts and employment contracts (excluded by the HCCH Principles' commercial scope)
The legal existence, powers and internal governance of the parties themselves (organization/person models)
The procurement or tendering process that precedes award
Conduct of litigation or arbitration proceedings and the resulting awards
Statutory and regulatory norms as such; only their declared applicability to this agreement is in scope
Payment execution, settlement instruments and accounting entries
Transfer of property/title, which CISG Article 4 expressly leaves to the applicable national law
Distributed-ledger execution substrates for smart contracts
Tax determination, transfer pricing and customs classification

boundary_notes.distinction: The tendering, evaluation and award process is owned by the procurement model; UBL separates Tender and Contract Award Notice documents from the resulting contract. Award output composes into a new agreement record here.

The legal entity and its verified identifier (LEI under ISO 17442) live in the party model; this model holds only the party position, its role and the link plus verification evidence. The registry validation flag 'a contract is not an organization' is upheld.

The arbitration or jurisdiction clause, the escalation state and the written-form evidence required by New York Convention Article II are in scope; the proceeding, award and enforcement action are not.

Overriding mandatory rules and statutory regimes (for example CISG applicability, unfair-term controls under the Data Act) are external norms; this model records only the applicability declaration and any opt-out.

Certificate issuance, trusted lists and signature-creation devices belong to the eIDAS trust-service domain; this model records the signature type, assurance level and validation evidence attached to execution.
Specialised agreement types EXTEND this model with domain terms and lifecycle events; their product-specific economics are not duplicated here.

functions.name: Register agreement record
functions.description: Create the jointly owned record for a new agreement with its identifier, party positions, classification and legal frame.
inputs: Party position set with role codes
preconditions: At least two party positions are declared
A commercial-scope assertion exists for every position
Governing law and forum are declared or explicitly marked absent
effects: Agreement identifier is bound and cannot be reassigned
Record enters the pre-effective state
Registration event is written to the audit log with event and ingestion time

functions.name: Verify party identity and signing authority
functions.description: Check each named party against the authoritative registry and confirm the signatory's power to bind within its limits.
preconditions: A party position exists
An authority basis is asserted
effects: Verification observation time is recorded
Authority defect raises an exception state instead of blocking silently

functions.name: Record conclusion and execution
functions.description: Capture the concluding communications or signatures, the effective moment and the signature validation evidence.
inputs: Formation communication set or signed container
preconditions: Party identity and authority verification have been attempted and their results recorded
Any applicable form requirement has been identified
effects: Executed expression digest is fixed and becomes immutable
Record moves to conditional or effective state depending on outstanding conditions

functions.name: Build addressable clause tree
functions.description: Convert the agreed text into a hierarchy of addressable provisions with expression and work identifiers and per-node digests.
preconditions: The manifestation's digest matches the executed expression digest
effects: Clause references become stable across later amendments
Any extraction uncertainty is recorded as provenance, not silently normalised

functions.name: Derive obligation set
functions.description: Produce deontic statements with bearers, conditions, violations and reparations traced to source clauses.
preconditions: Clause tree exists with stable identifiers
Bearer positions are resolvable
effects: Derived rules are marked as derived, never as the normative text
A later amendment invalidates and re-derives the affected rules

functions.name: Evaluate effectiveness and conditions
functions.description: Determine whether conditions precedent are satisfied or waived and compute the current validity state.
preconditions: Execution has been recorded
Each condition has an evidence slot
effects: Obligations become enforceable only after the effectiveness event
Lapse at long-stop date is recorded as an event, not a deletion

functions.name: Monitor due obligations
functions.description: Compute which duties are due, overdue or within a cure period from due conditions and recorded events.
preconditions: Obligations carry due conditions
All timestamps carry seconds and explicit offsets
effects: Status transitions are emitted as events with event and observation time
No status is inferred without an evidenced trigger

functions.name: Record performance and acceptance
functions.description: Attach evidence that a duty was performed, capture measured results and register the counterparty's acceptance decision.
preconditions: The obligation exists and is due or performable
The recording actor is authorised for that party position
effects: Event time and observation time are stored separately
Deemed acceptance is applied only where an agreed rule exists

functions.name: Declare non-performance and elect remedy
functions.description: Register a breach declaration, any asserted excuse, the remedy elected and its quantification.
preconditions: A notice satisfying the contractual notice rules has been issued where required
Any cure period has expired or is expressly waived
effects: Record enters a disputed state that blocks disposition
Remedy election is immutable once notified, subject to a superseding agreed settlement

functions.name: Apply executed amendment
functions.description: Produce a new expression of the agreed text from an executed amendment while retaining the superseded expression.
preconditions: The required variation formality is satisfied and evidenced
The amendment is signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution
effects: Superseded expression is retained and remains addressable
Obligations affected by changed clauses are invalidated and re-derived

functions.name: Issue and track formal notice
functions.description: Send a contractual notice through a permitted channel to the designated address and record dispatch, receipt and consequences.
preconditions: The channel and address are permitted by the contract
The sender is authorised to act for the sending position
effects: Notice periods start running from the deemed receipt time
Failure of delivery evidence marks the notice as contested rather than valid

functions.name: Verify record integrity
functions.description: Re-verify digests, signatures and time stamps over the executed text and dependent artifacts and report divergence.
preconditions: A canonicalisation rule is recorded for each artifact class
effects: Failed verification sets a disputed flag and never deletes the artifact
Verification observation time is recorded separately from the artifact's event time

functions.name: Emit projection to a non-party
functions.description: Generate a reduced view exposing only the elements a declared projection permits, with its omission list and generation time.
preconditions: A valid, unexpired grant covers the requested scope
The projection definition is a governed, versioned artifact
effects: Restricted elements are excluded before serialisation, not filtered afterwards
Every emission is logged with requester, purpose and grant reference

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Evaluate retention rules, limitation periods and holds, and carry out authorised disposition or redaction with evidence.
inputs: Limitation period for the governing law
preconditions: No hold or dispute is in force over the element
The longest applicable retention or limitation period has expired
effects: Executed text and signature evidence are never hard-deleted while any period runs
Redaction preserves the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control

functions.name: Avoid or terminate
functions.description: End the agreement by notice of avoidance, agreed termination or expiry, releasing future duties while preserving dispute and winding-up clauses and triggering restitution.
preconditions: fundamental breach, Nachfrist failure, agreed termination, or completed performance
notice given where CISG Article 26 requires it
effects: status becomes avoided or terminated
open primary obligations are released subject to damages and restitution

functions.name: Declare breach and fix additional time
functions.description: Record a breach declaration, classify it as fundamental or not, and optionally fix a Nachfrist period or demand adequate assurance.
preconditions: failure to perform or clear future fundamental breach
notice capable of reaching the other party
effects: inconsistent remedies are barred during a running Nachfrist
damages for delay remain available

functions.name: Assign or novate
functions.description: Transfer rights or, with required consent, obligations, and notify the remaining obligor without purporting to move in rem title.
preconditions: contractual assignability or required consent
notice to obligor where effectiveness against the obligor so requires
effects: party positions or payee identity change on the contractual plane only

composition.purpose: Resolve the legal entity occupying a party position and its governed identifier; entity existence and powers stay in the organization model.
Resolve natural persons acting as signatories or agents without duplicating personal data in the contract record.
Verify signing capacity and delegated powers against the constitutional documents recorded there.
An award concluded in the procurement model composes into a new agreement instance here; the tendering documents remain in the procurement model.
An insurance policy is a specialised commercial contract that extends this model with cover, premium and claim structures.
Executed prices may serve as price observations under a contribution agreement; the valuation model reads a projection rather than the terms.
Escalated disputes are heard there; this model holds the clause, the written-form evidence and the escalation state.
Joint ownership of the record and grants over scoped parts of it are administered by the stewardship and access-grant models.
Adds provenance and audit facets to execution, performance, amendment, notice and access events using a standard agent, activity and entity vocabulary.
Align the obligation model to a normative deontic vocabulary for obligations, permissions, prohibitions, violations and reparations.

composition.target: OASIS Akoma Ntoso and its Naming Convention v1.0
composition.purpose: Align clause addressing and versioned expression IRIs to an established legal-document naming convention.
Align exchange projections to interoperable business document types for contracting, ordering and delivery without exposing clause text.
Align formation, performance, non-performance, excuse and remedy terminology to the recognised international contract-law instruments.
Bind the delivery term data element to a governed classifier that requires both a rule code and an edition to be interpretable.

composition.target: Electronic signature and trust service framework
composition.purpose: Resolve signature assurance levels, certificates, time-stamp tokens and trusted-list status used as execution evidence.

owner_package_requirements: Declare a jointly owned record package per agreement instance in which each party position holds an equivalent mirror and joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events; unilateral acts such as notices are writable by their sender alone.
Bind every party position to an authoritative party record and store the identity verification evidence with its observation time before any obligation is derived.
Declare governing law, dispute forum and the retention jurisdiction before clause content is stored, because these determine mandatory rules, limitation periods and deletion limits.
Publish an AGENTS.md bootstrap and a versioned projection catalogue listing every view exposed to non-parties and what each view omits.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Adopt the namespace world.commercialContract under nav path NAV.SOC.ECO.CTR. Agreement expressions and clauses are named with FRBR-style Work and Expression IRIs and persistent clause identifiers so that references survive amendment; never mint contract IRIs under a single party's namespace, because the record is jointly owned. Derived artifacts such as obligation rule sets live in a clearly separate derived subnamespace so they can never be mistaken for the executed text.
registry_links: Global LEI Index for party legal entity identifiers under ISO 17442
ICC Incoterms rule codes with an explicit edition qualifier
Currency and country code lists referenced by the price, place-of-business and jurisdiction elements
Trusted lists of qualified trust service providers for signature and time-stamp validation
UBL document type and business process code lists used by exchange projections

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the executed expression: the clause tree with stable identifiers, the party positions, the derived obligation set marked as derived, and a digest over the normative text. PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, JSON, YAML and database rows are manifestations, not the canon.

Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; the local offset of execution, dispatch and delivery is preserved rather than normalised to Z, because contractual periods run in a stated locality.
Monetary values are canonicalised as an amount plus a currency code, never as formatted strings; quantities carry an explicit unit.
Parties are canonicalised to a position identifier plus a governed entity identifier, never to a display name; trade terms are canonicalised as code plus edition plus named place.
patch_rules: A patch that changes normative text is valid only if it carries an executed amendment instrument signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution.
Patches are append-only: superseded expressions are retained and remain addressable by their expression IRI; no in-place overwrite of executed content is permitted.
Editorial or metadata patches must be flagged non-normative and must not change the digest of the executed expression; if the digest would change, the change is an amendment, not a patch.
Every patch records the actor, the reason, the event time at which the change takes effect and the ingestion time at which it was recorded, as distinct values.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional findings, data elements or projections is backward compatible; changing the clause identity scheme, the deontic vocabulary, the party role vocabulary or the identity priority is breaking and requires a major version.
Relationships to CISG, UNIDROIT, Incoterms, UBL, LegalRuleML and Akoma Ntoso are published as alignments with a declared claim level; a conformance claim requires cited test evidence.
Consumers must tolerate unknown clause classes, unknown remedy kinds and unknown notice kinds rather than rejecting the record, and must not infer absence of a term from absence of a code.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the agreement, such as the contract register number of the register the parties have jointly designated as authoritative, where such an identifier exists and is agreed by all parties
Governed global identifier or IRI, such as a FRBR-style Akoma Ntoso expression IRI for the executed text or an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier for a party occupying a position
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting authority and mint time, used only where neither a master-system nor a governed identifier is available
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-times carrying seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; the local offset of execution, dispatch, delivery and performance is preserved because contractual periods run in a stated locality. Event time, meaning the moment the contractual fact occurred or took effect, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the moment the record captured it, whenever the two can differ. Where UTC is known but the local offset is not, use -00:00 rather than Z. A date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely amendments, notices, performance records, verification records, manifests, dispositions and log segments, are numbered with a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to the agreement identifier and the artifact class, for example agreement-id/amendment/0003. Sequence numbers are never reused, never renumbered on amendment and never encode a date; any effective date is carried as a separate field.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every executed or issued artifact carries a digest over its canonical bytes with a named algorithm, the signature or seal evidence relied on at execution, and an attributable time stamp. The digest of the executed expression is immutable for the life of the record. Verification failure sets a disputed flag, notifies all party positions and is written to the audit log; it never causes deletion or silent replacement of the artifact.

policies: Joint record policy: the agreement record is jointly owned by the party positions; joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events, while unilateral acts are attributable to their sender and remain contestable by the counterparty.
Alignment-not-conformance policy: relationships to external standards are recorded as alignments with an explicit claim level; a conformance claim without cited test evidence is a defect.

Derived-content policy: obligation rule sets, schedules, scorecards and summaries are marked as derived and carry provenance back to source clauses; they never acquire normative status over the executed text.
Minimisation policy: any view issued to a non-party exposes only what its versioned projection definition permits and publishes the list of what it omits.

Preservation policy: retention rules are suspended by a dispute or legal hold; personal data inside executed evidence is redacted in place with preserved digests rather than destroyed while any limitation period runs.
Party-mirror policy: each party holds the full agreement record; joint facts change only by joint events or jointly authorized amendments.

Form-and-signature policy: writing and signature requirements follow the applicable instrument (CISG Articles 11–13 and 96, UCC § 2-201, MLEC/MLES) and any insisted particular form under UNIDROIT Article 2.1.13.
Disclosure-minimisation policy: existence and performance standing may be disclosed to consented credit or rating consumers; clause text and prices are omitted from public summaries.
No-unilateral-delete policy: the joint record is not deleted by a single party's CRUD delete; retention, legal hold and limitation clocks govern archive and redaction.

read: Every party position may read the complete joint record, including clause text, obligations and performance history.
Non-parties read only through a declared projection, and the projection definition is itself a governed, versioned artifact.
Reads of restricted findings such as price terms, liability caps and personal data are logged with requester identity, purpose and grant reference.
create: Creating an agreement record requires at least two party positions, a subject-matter class, a governing-law declaration and a recorded conclusion or execution event with evidence.
Clause, obligation, milestone, performance, notice and amendment records may be created only under an existing agreement identifier.
Creation resolves the identifier through the identity priority; a Dimension-minted surrogate is permitted only with recorded minting authority and mint time.
update: Changes to normative content require an executed amendment artifact; the prior expression is retained and stays addressable.
Operational changes such as performance, notices, status transitions and disclosures are recorded as append-only events, never as in-place edits.
Metadata corrections are recorded as non-normative patches carrying actor, reason, event time and ingestion time, and must not alter the executed expression digest.
delete: Hard deletion of executed text, signature evidence, notices or performance evidence is prohibited while any limitation period, statutory retention duty or legal hold applies.
Personal data within executed evidence may be redacted in place, with a redaction record preserving the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control.
Disposition after retention expiry follows an approved disposition authority and is itself recorded as an event with its authorising instrument.

roles.name: Party record steward
responsibilities: Maintain one party's mirror of the joint record and keep it reconciled with the counterparty's mirror
Escalate divergence between mirrors as a dispute rather than resolving it unilaterally

roles.name: Authorised representative
responsibilities: Execute, amend, assign or terminate on behalf of a party within recorded authority limits
Ensure the authority instrument relied on is current and evidenced at the time of signing

roles.name: Contract text custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the clause tree, expression versions, document manifest and precedence order
Preserve superseded expressions and the identifier map that links them

roles.name: Performance recorder and verifier
responsibilities: Record performance events, measured values and acceptance decisions with event and observation times
Attach evidence and flag deemed acceptance only where an agreed rule exists

roles.name: Access and disclosure administrator
responsibilities: Issue, scope and expire grants over bundles, layers, findings and artifacts
Apply redaction rules and log every disclosure with purpose and legal basis

roles.name: Records and retention officer
responsibilities: Apply retention rules, limitation periods and legal holds and block disposition while any is in force
Execute and evidence authorised disposition or redaction

access.default_rule: Deny by default to anyone who is not a party position. Each party position has full read of the joint record, write on its own unilateral acts, and no unilateral write on joint facts, which require joint evidence.
exceptions: Adjudication access: a court or arbitral tribunal obtains the record once a dispute is escalated under the agreed forum clause
Regulatory or tax authority access on a stated legal basis, with the parties notified unless notification is prohibited
Auditor, financier or prospective assignee due diligence under a time-limited grant, normally on a redacted projection
Statutory disclosure duties, including unfair-term and data-sharing controls, that override a confidentiality clause
Emergency continuity access by a designated custodian where a party's system is unavailable, logged and reviewed afterwards
Adjudication access after a dispute is escalated to the contractual forum
Consented counterparty-status disclosure of existence and coarse performance standing to credit or rating consumers
Public-summary projection of existence, parties and subject-matter class where a transparency register is agreed or required
Mandatory regulatory disclosure that is an overriding mandatory rule of the forum
audit_requirements: Log every read of a restricted finding or artifact with requester, purpose, grant reference and timestamp carrying an explicit offset
Log grant issuance, scope, expiry and revocation as first-class events
Keep the audit log append-only and tamper-evident, with each segment chained to the digest of its predecessor
Retain audit entries at least as long as the record element they describe, and never dispose of them earlier

Log execution, amendment, performance acceptance, breach declaration, avoidance, assignment and every access exception with actor, artifact, event time and ingestion time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Preserve content hashes of each expression so that later projections can be verified
Record who opened adjudication access and under which dispute-clause identifier

required_fields: Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to learn the model name, entry kind and the four resolution URLs
Follow the Specification URL to load the bundle, layer, finding and question structure and the identity and timestamp rules
Follow the Storage type URL to learn the concrete projection in use, whether documents, rows, graph nodes or files, and its canonicalisation rules
Follow the Interface URL to learn the read, create, update and delete operations available and their scopes
Follow the Processes URL for formation, performance, amendment, notice, dispute and disposition procedures
Read the Projection Catalogue URL before emitting anything to a non-party, and the Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL before asserting any legal consequence

coverage.claim: Base claude structure, plus two grok findings, covers agreement identity and legal frame, party positions and authority, formation and execution, agreed text and commercial terms, the obligation/performance/variance lifecycle, and record governance for business-to-business commercial agreements as grounded in the cited instruments. Coverage is asserted only for the sourced instruments and the profiles actually tested; it is not a universal or complete account of commercial contracting, national validity law, or any sector profile, and no conformance to any cited standard is claimed without test evidence.

checklist.notes: Agreement identity, instance boundary and expression addressing are a dedicated finding; party identity uses a governed global identifier; the identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first and excludes dates as identifiers.
